Power is provided by an air-cooled 1,170cc opposed-twin paired with a five-speed transmission, and equipment includes an enclosed driveshaft, dual external oil coolers, electronic fuel injection, a Staintune two-into-two exhaust system, a Telelever front end, a Paralever single-sided swingarm, triple anti-lock disc brakes, wire-spoke wheels, a clear windscreen, navy blue-upholstered two-up seating, rider and passenger backrests, folding passenger foot pegs, leather-covered side cases, and a side stand. Now indicating 16k miles, this R1200C is offered at no reserve with a tool kit, factory literature, a September 2026 service invoice, and a California title in the seller's name.

articles.title: HEADLINES: DFA dresses down China’s envoy Jing | October 20, 2026
articles.description: Good day. Here are the stories of The Manila Times for Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Today’s episode is brought to you by Wilcon Depot, The Philippines’ leading home improvement and construction supplies retailer — your Trusted Building Partner. BANNER: DFA dresses down China’s envoy Jing FOREIGN Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro on Monday summoned Chinese Ambassador Jing Quan to express the Philippines’ strong objection to his public statement which conveyed “a threat of the use of force.” Lazaro told Jing that his Oct. 15 statement, in which he said China could “easily win” if it chose to use force against the Philippines in their ongoing maritime dispute, was “provocative and unacceptable, and does not contribute to creating understanding,” the DFA said in a statement. The DFA called out Jing for issuing a “thinly veiled threat of the use of force” in addressing the maritime dispute between the Philippines and China. During a chance interview at the sidelines of the Second Diliman Dialogue on China-Philippines relations, Jing reportedly said that if the two sides were to become embroiled in conflict and confrontation, China “may easily win, but we will not use force, as we love peace.” Tulfo hurt by three senators’ bid to unseat him SEN. Erwin Tulfo on Monday admitted he was hurt and saddened by the reported votes of three minority senators who opposed the dismissal of a motion seeking to revive a petition challenging his eligibility to remain in the Senate. Tulfo identified Sens. Pia Cayetano, Camille Villar and Robinhood Padilla as the three minority bloc members of the Senate Electoral Tribunal (SET) who reportedly voted in favor of the appeal, which was defeated 6-3 on Oct. 16. He said he was particularly disappointed with Villar and Padilla, with whom he had maintained cordial relations. Tulfo said he and Padilla would greet each other and refer to one another as “insan” because of their distant family ties. He also said he had previously exchanged greetings and jokes with Villar, with whom he had worked in Congress. As for Cayetano, Tulfo said he had anticipated her position because they had not been on speaking terms for some time. CIDG subpoenas over 21 people in Laos case THE Philippine National Police (PNP) has subpoenaed more than 21 people to shed light on their alleged involvement or knowledge of the foiled attempt to smuggle in P3.5 billion worth of shabu from Laos. Col. Allen Rae Co, PNP spokesman, said the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG) has issued the subpoenas to those “not necessarily involved directly” so they can “exercise their right to be heard.” In a press briefing at Camp Crame on Monday, Co said more persons will be subpoenaed in the coming days. He also requested the subpoenaed persons to bring the required documents that are needed in the questioning. Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on Monday dared critics to challenge him on the facts of the case being built in connection to the multibillion drug haul. Marcoleta suspended over plunder charge THE Sandiganbayan Third Division has ordered the 90-day preventive suspension of detained Sen. Rodante Marcoleta over his pending P75-million plunder case. Third Division Clerk of Court Dennis Pulma confirmed the Oct. 19 ruling promulgated by Associate Justice Karl B. Miranda, on Oct. 19, to The Manila Times on Monday. The plunder case accuses Marcoleta of amassing P75 million in ill-gotten wealth through alleged gifts or donations of P30 million from Mike Defensor, P25 million from Joseph Espiritu and P20 million from Aristotle Baluyut Viray, purportedly received by reason of his former position as Sagip party-list representative. 50K homes up for grabs at biggest housing expo MORE than 50,000 housing units are being showcased by over 80 property developers at the country’s biggest National Housing Expo, offering Filipino families more choices and access to subsidized home loans under the administration’s Expanded 4PH housing program. The two-day expo, which opened Monday, Oct. 19, at the SMX Convention Center Manila in Pasay City, brings major real estate developers and government housing agencies under one roof to make homeownership more accessible. Organized by the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) and Pag-IBIG Fund, the event is part of the celebration of National Shelter Month and the largest edition of the government-led housing expo to date. BUSINESS: Peso drops to new low THE peso plunged to a new record low of P63.09 against the greenback on Monday as the dollar strengthened against major currencies due to geopolitical uncertainties. The local currency weakened by ten and a half centavos to P63.06 from Friday’s P62.985:$1. This is the weakest close since Oct. 15’s P63.06:$1. The peso opened at P62.98 and traded between P62.98 and P63.17:$1. The volume reached P1.778 billion, higher than the previous P1.598 billion. Philippine Institute for Development Studies (PIDS) senior fellow John Paolo Rivera said the recent weakness reflects a “persistent dollar strength, elevated oil prices, geopolitical uncertainty, and increased demand for foreign currency.” SPORTS: Carlos Yulo eyes double gold finish at Worlds CARLOS Yulo looks to add another medal to his collection when he conquers the vault and floor exercise events at the 2026 FIG Artistic Gymnastics World Championships in Rotterdam. Fresh off winning a double gold medal in the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the two-time Olympic gold medalist is set to conquer the Rotterdam mats, eyeing another golden finish. Yulo displayed his caliber and placed second in the floor exercise event with 14.500 points and sixth on vault with 14.266 points to book a finals slot. The floor exercise final is slated for Oct. 24, while the vault final is scheduled for Oct. 25. Opinion and Editorial Antonio Contreras and Orlando Mercado are today’s front page columnists. Contreras’ column is about what he calls the persecution theater of Vice President Sara Duterte. Yen Makabenta discussed the evolution of Presidential communications while former senator Mercado’s topic is about the future without political surnames. Today’s editorial is about the need for so-called ‘third spaces’ in Metro Manila.
